newsitem.title: INDIA: DELHI SHARES EDGE UP ON DEFERRED OIL PRICE RISE.
newsitem.headline: DELHI SHARES EDGE UP ON DEFERRED OIL PRICE RISE.

text.p: Delhi shares quoted modestly higher in early trade on Thursday as speculators made selective purchases, fuelled by the ruling United Front's decision to defer a decision on whether to raise oil prices, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's Sensitive Index was 1.58 points higher at 924.48 after 30 minutes of trade.
The coalition on Wednesday postponed a decision on whether to raise domestic petroleum prices but said it would soon have to increase prices despite stiff communist opposition.
Brokers also attributed the rise in share prices to short covering by speculators ahead of Friday's fortnightly settlement.
"The volume of business was low as players confined themselves to the trend-setter Reliance Industries and a few other stocks," said Vinod Chadha of brokers Top-Tips Investments.
Larsen and Toubro firmed 2.45 rupees to 275.
State Bank of India gained 0.30 rupee to 323.
